title: Realizable Nearlinear-Gap Hardness for Small Monotone Formulas
description:
For every sufficiently large fixed leaf bound L, this manuscript proves randomized polynomial-time many-one NP-hardness of realizable weighted Collection Minimum Monotone Satisfying Assignment with gap L^(1-o(1)) and a vanishing NO satisfaction threshold. Hirahara--Nanashima's transfer gives the corresponding fixed-advice realizable learning corollary. The polynomial exponent may depend on L. This establishes the epsilon=0 strengthening asked in Section 7 of their June 23, 2026 revision.

Earlier realizable hardness is credited to Hirahara; the contribution is the nearlinear exponent. The proof combines established Grassmann PCP machinery and compilation/learning reductions with an explicit parameter, posterior, threshold-ladder and completeness-repair argument. The complete proof, exact source contracts and review disclosures are included.

Informal AI derivation and independent agent review; no independent human peer review, Lean verification or priority certification is claimed. The MZ publisher full text was inaccessible in the assessment; numerical observations concern the cited arXiv v1. No growing-parameter theorem, linear-factor hardness, one-way-function construction or P-versus-NP resolution is claimed.
notes: Version 0.1.0 corrects the initial GitHub label 1.0.0 to a sub-1 research-preprint version. The historical v1.0.0 tag and release are preserved. Mathematical content and review findings are unchanged; this release adds archive metadata.
